subject: ACME order form — indemnity carveout and escrow trigger discussion
messages:
From: Susan Clark <susan.clark@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2025-08-18 09:12 -0700
Subject: Order form question — indemnity for model output

Hi Rachel,

We're finalizing the order form for the pilot and our legal team flagged the indemnity section. Specifically: if a third party alleges IP infringement caused by model-generated output (text or code), Acme needs clarity on whether Redwood will 'defend' or only 'reimburse', and what activation triggers are required (notice + final judgment vs. notice alone).

Procurement is pushing to avoid an open-ended defense obligation — they're asking for either: (a) reimbursement-only with a clear cap, or (b) a defense-with-control limited to third-party patent claims only.

Can you share Redwood's preferred approach and any suggested compromises? Also please attach any SOC2 / evidence we can use in our risk review. We're on a compressed timeline — procurement would like a final position by next week.

Thanks,
Susan
Susan Clark
Sr. Procurement Manager — Acme Corp

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-18 11:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form question — indemnity for model output

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear outline and the PO. Looping in our legal lead Kimberly and Ben from sales ops so we can move quickly.

High level: Redwood's starting point is defense-with-control for third-party patent claims and will offer reimbursement for other IP claims tied specifically to model outputs (copyright/style disputes). That said, we understand procurement's risk tolerance and are open to a sublimit and clearer activation triggers.

I've attached a proposed redline of the MSA/order form showing the following options we can present to Acme's counsel:
- Defense-with-control for third-party patents only; Redwood to control defense and settlement, with obligation to keep Acme reasonably informed.
- Reimbursement-only for other IP allegations (e.g., alleged copyright in generated text) with a per-claim cap.
- Escrow/insurance trigger options: (i) escrow activation only after final judgment or insurer denial; (ii) provisional deposit on notice + escrow release path.

Can you confirm which of the two escrow trigger approaches procurement prefers? Also, please confirm Acme's risk tolerance for a per-claim cap (ballpark number would help).

I'll let Kimberly propose concrete language.

Best,
Rachel
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Acme_MSA_redline.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Susan Clark <susan.clark@acme.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-19 09:20 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form question — indemnity for model output

Hi all — Kimberly from Redwood Legal here. Quick read-through and a proposed compromise below; attaching a clean proposal for counsel to review.

Principles: limit Redwood's exposure for model-output claims where Redwood does not have control over the customer prompt/application; provide Acme with evidence and an operational notice/cure flow; and ensure activation triggers are not so onerous they leave Acme unprotected.

Proposed terms (summary):
1) Defense scope: Redwood will defend and control the defense for third-party patent infringement claims arising directly from the operation of Redwood-hosted models. Redwood will not accept control for non-patent IP allegations (copyright, trademark) — those will be rebuttable reimbursement obligations.
2) Sublimit: a per-claim monetary sublimit of $750,000 for all model-output related IP claims (this is negotiable; suggests compromise between your ask and our exposure).
3) Evidence and cooperation: Acme must (a) provide prompt notice, (b) preserve relevant logs/prefixes, (c) produce reasonable technical evidence per the evidence checklist in §3 of the attachment.
4) Escrow/insurance trigger: escrow activation only after final adjudication or insurer denial; alternative provisional funding (10% holdback) on notice can be negotiated.
5) Cure window: 30 days from notice for Acme to identify mitigation steps; if mitigation reasonably addresses the claim, parties will coordinate before escrow activation.

Attaching: Redwood_indemnity_proposal_v1.docx (tracked language + evidence checklist).

Questions for Acme: can procurement live with defense-only for PATENTS and reimbursement for other IP? If not, what cap would they need for reimbursement-only? Also please confirm whether Acme can provide the architecture diagram and SOC2 snapshot noted in Rachel's note — those materially reduce our risk and make the sublimit workable.

Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_indemnity_proposal_v1.docx
From: Susan Clark <susan.clark@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, legal-team@acme.com
Date: 2025-08-19 15:50 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form question — indemnity for model output

Kimberly / Rachel — thanks for the fast turnaround and the clear proposal. A few notes from Acme legal/procurement after internal review: 

- Procurement cannot accept an open defense-with-control for all IP allegations. Their preference is reimbursement-only capped at $500k for all model-output claims.
- Legal is willing to consider a hybrid approach (defense-with-control for third-party PATENTS; reimbursement for copyright/trademark) but would like the per-claim cap to be $1,000,000.
- Regarding escrow: our commercial team prefers escrow activation only after final judgment or if Redwood's insurer denies coverage. The provisional funding option (10% holdback) is palatable if Redwood can commit to a maximum 90-day escrow resolution timeline.
- Attached is our SOC snapshot and a short architecture note for the evaluation team.

Can Redwood confirm whether the $750k sublimit is flexible toward $1M and whether you can accept the 90-day timeline for provisional funding release? Also can you share the evidence checklist referenced in Kimberly's doc (we need it to see what logs/data we'll be asked to provide).

Best,
Susan
Sr. Procurement Manager — Acme Corp
Attachment: Acme_SOC2_snapshot.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Susan Clark <susan.clark@acme.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-20 16:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form question — indemnity for model output — proposed path forward

Thanks everyone — Ben from Sales Ops. Quick proposed path to keep the deal moving while protecting both sides: 

1) Compromise indemnity language: defense-with-control for third-party PATENT infringement only; reimbursement for other IP claims tied to model output. Set per-claim sublimit at $750,000 but add a negotiation carve allowing Acme to raise to $1,000,000 for enterprise customers with confirmed SOC2 + architecture diagram.
2) Escrow/insurance: Redwood accepts escrow activation after final judgment or insurer denial. For provisional funding, Redwood will agree to a 10% holdback on initial invoice with a maximum 90-day escrow resolution SLA (Redwood will provide weekly status updates to Acme).
3) Evidence checklist: Kimberly's attachment contains the checklist. We'll extract the checklist into a short operational handoff doc (what logs, prefixes, timeframe) in the next 48 hours and post to HubSpot.
4) Timeline: Redwood will circulate a revised redline (v2) with the compromise language by 2025-08-22. If Acme agrees, we aim to finalize counters and route for signature via DocuSign by 2025-09-05.

Action items:
- Redwood legal (Kimberly) to produce redline v2 and extracted checklist (due 8/22).
- Acme to confirm whether the $750k floor + enterprise raise to $1M is acceptable and to confirm procurement contact for the 10% holdback.
- Rachel to update HubSpot with action plan and attach the docs.
